scope: Pinned public IDX-derived EOD and IPO snapshots; capability and authority-boundary research only

idx_api_source_discovery.live_probe: initial ordinary curl to the legacy official host/endpoint received HTTP 403 Cloudflare challenge; no authenticated/provider call was made; a later ordinary idx.id current-directory GET is recorded separately

what_is_proven: CNTX is discoverable in two independent public ticker-file snapshots, so its panel absence is not universal absence from available public EOD sources.

The six anchor/panel tickers absent from the May-29 EOD snapshot exactly match the IPO dataset's declared new-stock list updated June 28, 2026; this explains the observed snapshot timing gap as a bounded, independently supported hypothesis.
Public EOD rows cover approximately 99.75% of frozen anchor/panel keys through the public snapshot date, but residual missing keys remain and the source is not population-complete by contract.
The public EOD source contains raw volume/OHLC/share/name fields and visible zero-volume or zero-OHLC patterns, but field presence is not event, identity, PIT, or corporate-action authority.

The official current directory independently confirms the six newer codes and their July 7-10, 2026 listing dates, while the 18 anchor-only historical codes remain outside the current directory; this resolves only the current-snapshot comparison, not historical population completeness.
what_remains_unknown: historical population completeness and survivorship safety
issuer/ISIN continuity, ticker reuse, delisted/relisted lifecycle completeness
corporate-action effective transition and price-basis semantics
whether the public snapshots omit any population outside their ticker-file sets

admission.allowed_use: source capability, gap explanation, and future acquisition design only
admission.forbidden_use: canonical substitution, backfill, eligibility authority, or predictive admission

reopen_trigger: An authoritative population-wide PIT security master or equivalent contract with issuer/ISIN lifecycle, publication/knowledge time, corporate-action basis, and revision semantics.
